title: Normalized generic trivialization and geometric lifts for a constructible module sheaf
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], Lambda a finite commutative ring, F a constructible sheaf of Lambda-modules on the small etale site of X [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and x a point of X. There exist a scheme Y, an integral morphism nu:Y -> X [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], a field K, a morphism g:Spec K -> Y, and a finite Lambda-module M such that the unit M_Y -> g_*g^*M_Y is an isomorphism, and g^*nu^*F is isomorphic to g^*M_Y [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Moreover every geometric point s:Spec Omega -> X above x [def-weil-geometric-point] factors as w followed by g and nu for some w:Spec Omega -> Spec K. No morphism F -> nu_*M_Y is part of the data.

proof.text: Pull back F to Spec kappa(x). Pull the finite locally closed stratification back, including constructibility of its subsets. Convert each finite-value trivialization to finite locally constant, use pullback stability, then convert back with finite_locally_constant_module_values_iff. Apply the field trivialization theorem to obtain a finite separable K/kappa(x), finite M and an isomorphism on Spec K.

Noetherian X is quasi-separated. Normalize X in Spec K using the finite residue-field extension theorem, obtaining integral nu:Y -> X, normal integral Y, and g:Spec K -> Y whose composite with nu is the residue-field map and whose image is generic with residue-field isomorphism. Compose inverse images and the constant pullback comparison to identify g^*nu^*F with g^*M_Y.

Apply the normal constant generic theorem to M_Y. Its Lean interface uses the canonical spectrum of the generic local ring. Factor g through the spectrum of the residue field at its image, using the residue-field description of field-valued points. Its residue-field map is an isomorphism, and the quotient from the generic local ring to its residue field is an isomorphism since that local ring is a field. Thus g differs from the canonical generic inclusion by an isomorphism of source schemes. The adjunction for a scheme isomorphism is an equivalence; composition of inverse images and uniqueness of adjoints transport the invertible unit to g. This gives precisely the unit isomorphism in the conclusion.

For an algebraically closed Omega and s above x, its residue-field homomorphism kappa(x) -> Omega extends to K by the algebraic-extension embedding theorem. Take Spec of this extension to obtain w. Compatibility over kappa(x), the residue-field description of s, and g followed by nu equal to the original residue-field morphism show w followed by g and nu equals s. This gives every required lift. The empty base has no x; for the zero sheaf take M=0.

theorem exists_constructible_module_normalized_generic_data
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hF : Scheme.IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf F) (x : X) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (ν : Y ⟶ X), IsIntegralHom ν ∧
      ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Y)
        (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ), Finite M ∧
        IsIso ((upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).unit.app
          ((constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M)) ∧
        Nonempty
          ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).obj
            ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ν).obj F) ≅
           (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).obj
            ((constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M)) ∧
        ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X),
          ((Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField Ω X) s).1 = x →
            ∃ w : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec (.of K), w ≫ g ≫ ν = s
